channel.title: Space Digest
channel.description: The podcasts worth your week, in a minute each.

item.title: What Anthropic’s IPO Filing Reveals
item.description: Anthropic’s IPO filing shows a company growing at record speed while betting hundreds of billions on AI infrastructure.

item.title: The Space Technology That Could Change History Forever
item.description: A company wants to turn rockets into giant orbital power plants and data centers.

item.title: The Secret Government Operation Faking Alien Abductions
item.description: The episode argues that UFOs, psychic research, and alien abductions may be tools in a hidden human control system.

item.title: Reinventing School for the AI Era | Joe Liemandt, Gagan Biyani & Erik Torenberg
item.description: The most useful school of the AI era may look less like school—and demand much more from students.

item.title: What Everyone Gets Wrong About Porn Addiction (Jay Stringer) | Ep. 602
item.description: Porn recovery works better when it uncovers the pain beneath desire and builds a life worth staying present for.

item.title: OpenAI: When AI Agents Use Computers Faster Than You
item.description: AI agents are moving from clicking through software to running entire workflows faster than people.

item.title: Introducing How We Got Here -- NLW's new podcast
item.description: Data centers became a political flashpoint because Americans stopped trusting the tech industry long before AI arrived.

item.title: 4 Questions for AI This Week
item.description: AI’s biggest risks may now be arriving faster than labs can contain them.

item.title: #351 Chris Hansen - Hollywood’s To Catch a Predator Movie: “They Make Me Look Like a Vampire”
item.description: Online predators can look ordinary, move fast, and find children almost anywhere.

item.title: 323. Why Getting Things Done Isn’t Enough
item.description: Getting things done can produce perfect results while quietly making you less loving.

item.title: The New Startup Playbook | Box CEO Aaron Levie
item.description: AI may let tiny startups match giants, but judgment, taste, and distribution still decide who wins.

item.title: How I'm Actually Using AI Right Now (Including Claude Duet)
item.description: Personal AI agents sound powerful, but the real breakthrough may be simpler: turning AI into a sharper thinking partner.

item.title: What It Takes to Win as a Founder | Ben Horowitz
item.description: AI may make companies easier to build, but it does not make founding one easier.

item.title: The Most Concerning AI Bubble Signals
item.description: The biggest AI bubble risk may not be unused chips or debt, but whether today’s customers keep paying.

item.title: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy on Why Amazon Is Investing $220 Billion in AI
item.description: Amazon says AI is growing far faster than its cloud business did—and could shrink many familiar teams.

item.title: #2570 - Mystery Boys
item.description: The episode argues that hidden systems—from AI to targeted ads—can quietly reshape what people believe and how they behave.

item.title: The Frontier Ideas a16z Wants to Fund | Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz & Chris Dixon
item.description: AI is moving so fast that startups, hardware, and the internet may all need to be rebuilt around it.

item.title: The AI vs AI Battle for the Internet
item.description: The internet is entering an era where AI attackers and defenders race at machine speed—and coordination may decide who wins.

item.title: Muslims Are Going to Priests for Exorcisms (Fr. Anthony Mourad) | Last Call Ep. 37
item.description: Muslims in Egypt sometimes seek Coptic priests for exorcisms, while Christians must evangelize through trust and example.

item.title: JRE MMA Show #187 with Robert Whittaker
item.description: Elite fighting is shown less as nonstop violence than as managing damage, family, fear, and the right time to change.

item.title: #350 Mike Hayes - The Navy SEAL in Obama’s Situation Room During the Captain Phillips Rescue
item.description: A Navy SEAL’s biggest lessons came from choosing restraint, protecting people, and admitting what he did not know.

item.title: Top Religious Scholar: “Aliens Aren’t What You Think!”
item.description: Aliens may be less about outer space than about trauma, sexuality, consciousness, and a reality humans barely understand.

item.title: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agents: Documents | Reducto’s Adit Abraham
item.description: AI agents may reason well, but they still need a dependable way to read the messy documents behind real work.

item.title: How AI Is Changing What Work Means
item.description: AI may change work most by letting ordinary firms tackle problems far outside their usual business.

item.title: #2569 - Bill Thompson
item.description: The episode links hunting, addiction, dreams, fighting, and AI through one idea: control is always temporary.

item.title: Why AI Companies Are Betting Personality Beats Intelligence
item.description: AI companies may win users less by thinking harder than by feeling better to talk with.

item.title: What Happens When Everyone Has a Health Expert in Their Pocket? | OpenAI’s Karan Singhal
item.description: AI may change healthcare most by helping people avoid costly problems before they need treatment.

item.title: My Unredacted Interview with The Leah Files
item.description: The episode alleges that money, influence, and surveillance systems are quietly linking politics, private firms, and foreign interests.

item.title: #2568 - Ross Edgley
item.description: Ross Edgley treats pain, danger, and even failure as problems that purpose can overpower.

item.title: What Happens When Al Agents Can Spend Your Money?
item.description: AI agents may reshape software by doing the work between apps, not merely answering questions.

item.title: The Miracle of Our Lady of Zeitoun (Fr. Anthony Mourad) | Ep. 601
item.description: A Marian apparition witnessed by crowds, investigated by authorities, and never heard speaking became a source of Christian unity.

item.title: The AI Wealth Problem
item.description: AI may create enormous wealth, but the real fight is over who controls and shares it.

item.title: #349 AJ Gentile - Grand Canyon Conspiracies, AI Extinction and Nuclear War on Mars
item.description: Mars, AI, UFOs, and ancient civilizations become one sprawling argument about what humanity thinks it knows.

item.title: 322. How to Actually Follow Through on Your Plans
item.description: Most people do not fail because their plan is bad; they fail because they never truly launch it.

item.title: Why Real-World AI Is Harder Than the Benchmark | EliseAI’s Mario Martone
item.description: Real-world AI is harder than lab benchmarks because a small error rate becomes millions of failures affecting people’s lives.

item.title: A Potentially Historic AI Breakthrough
item.description: A once-pessimistic researcher now says most AI systems may be readable—and larger models could be easier to understand.

item.title: Why AI Could Finally Fix Healthcare Access | Zocdoc CEO Oliver Kharraz
item.description: Healthcare access may improve by opening more doors—not forcing every patient through one.

item.title: The Most Important AI News This Week Is Getting Overlooked
item.description: The quietest model releases may matter most because they give businesses cheaper, more private ways to use AI.

item.title: Has the Catholic Church Changed Its Teaching on the Death Penalty?
item.description: The Church’s new death-penalty language may reject executions without clearly declaring them evil in every age.

item.title: AI Can Write the Code. Can It Run the System? | Grepr CEO Jad Naous
item.description: AI can write production code quickly, but surviving real-world system chaos is the harder test.

item.title: #2567 - Mariana van Zeller
item.description: Scams thrive not because victims are foolish, but because loneliness, profit and weak safeguards make deception powerful.

item.title: When AI Agents Start Spending Your Money | Alex Rampell & Terry Angelos
item.description: AI agents are moving from suggesting purchases to spending money, but the payment rules are still unfinished.

item.title: The 4 Ways the Devil Tries to Destroy You | Msgr. Charles Pope | Last Call Ep. 36
item.description: The devil’s most effective attacks may look like truth, political outrage, self-doubt, or even religious devotion.

item.title: How the Latest AI Leap Is Disrupting Business Models
item.description: AI is moving from making software faster to making the old software business model unstable.

item.title: #348 Frank Wright - The Last Living Original Marine Raider From WW2
item.description: A teenage recruit survived brutal Pacific fighting, but his hardest battle may have come after the war.

item.title: #2566 - Cody Tucker
item.description: A flood of strange facts reveals how easily trusted stories, institutions, and online outrage can hide something darker.

item.title: What Gemini 4 Argon Is Actually Good For
item.description: Gemini 4 Argon looks less like a coding champion and more like a surprisingly useful creative generalist.

item.title: Can Open Models Keep Up With the AI Frontier? | Nathan Lambert
item.description: Open models may trail the frontier, but cheaper compute and shared research could still reshape who wins.

item.title: “AI Is ALIEN Technology!” -Whistleblower Reveals TRUTH
item.description: AI may not just change physics—it could force humanity to rethink consciousness, intelligence, and even what counts as life.

item.title: #2565 - Michael Douglas
item.description: Michael Douglas links cancer, nuclear weapons, psychedelics, drug smuggling, and career-defining risks to one lesson: keep choosing boldly.
